record.paper_title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can reinforcement-learning agents use counterfactual inference for decision-making, such as less biased policy search, credit assignment in multi-agent systems, or human-in-the-loop action reasoning, despite the difficulty of learning correct structural causal models?

evidence.quote: Counterfactual Decision-Making: Bareinboim [213] expose that inference of counterfactuals is neglected in the RL literature, possibly due to the difficulty of learning correct SCMs.

However, counterfactual reasoning in agents may bring additional benefits to agents only reasoning based on observational distributions, such as less bias during policy search (Sec. 7.5), assigning credit to single agents in a shared-reward cooperative multi-agent system [284] or considering the intended actions of humans in a human-in-the-loop system [322].
We hope to see more carefully-designed counterfactual agents for real-world systems that may take inspiration from Bottou et al. [208].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a sequential decision-making setting modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) M = (S, A, P, R, gamma) augmented with a structural causal model (SCM) M_C = (U, V, F, P(U)), where U is a set of exogenous noise variables with distribution P(U), V is a set of endogenous variables including the state S_t, action A_t, and reward R_t at each time t, and F = {f_V : V in V} is a set of structural assignments such that each endogenous variable V is determined by its causal parents pa(V) subset V union U via V = f_V(pa(V)). For any intervention do(A_t = a) and any observed trajectory tau = (s_0, a_0, r_0, ..., s_T, a_T, r_T), the counterfactual distribution P(Y_{A_t = a} | tau) is defined by (i) abduction: updating P(U) to P(U | tau); (ii) action: replacing the structural assignment for A_t with the constant a; (iii) prediction: computing the distribution of Y in the modified SCM under the updated noise distribution.

Develop a reinforcement-learning framework in which an agent uses such counterfactual queries for decision-making, and address the following concrete sub-problems:

1. (Policy search with reduced bias.) Given a behavior policy pi_b and a target policy pi_theta parameterized by theta, design an estimator J_CF(theta) of the expected return J(theta) = E_{pi_theta}[sum_t gamma^t R_t] that uses counterfactual outcomes computed from trajectories generated by pi_b, and prove conditions on the SCM (e.g., identifiability of counterfactuals, ignorability of unobserved confounders) under which J_CF(theta) has strictly smaller bias and/or variance than standard importance-sampling off-policy estimators.

2. (Counterfactual credit assignment in cooperative multi-agent RL.) For n agents with joint action A_t = (A_t^1, ..., A_t^n) sharing a single team reward R_t, define for each agent i a counterfactual contribution C_t^i = E[R_t | tau] - E[R_t | do(A_t^i = a_0^i), tau] for a chosen baseline action a_0^i, and give learning algorithms that (a) estimate C_t^i consistently from trajectories and (b) yield policy-gradient updates whose variance is provably lower than the centralized-critic baseline while preserving the policy-gradient theorem in expectation.

3. (Human-in-the-loop counterfactual reasoning.) Suppose at certain times a human provides an intended action A_t^H which may differ from the agent's executed action A_t. Formalize how an agent should compute and act on counterfactual queries of the form "what would the return have been had the agent executed A_t^H instead of A_t?", and characterize when incorporating such queries improves sample efficiency or alignment with the human's intent.

4. (Learning the SCM from interaction.) Provide sample-complexity guarantees, or impossibility results, for learning, from online interaction with the environment, an SCM that is sufficient to identify the counterfactual quantities used in (1)–(3).

The problem is to develop such a framework and establish the corresponding theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms.
artifact.status_search_result: Counterfactual reasoning in reinforcement learning is an active research area with partial results (e.g., counterfactual multi-agent policy gradients/COMA, counterfactual credit assignment papers, and works by Bareinboim and collaborators on causal RL), but a unified framework addressing less-biased policy search, multi-agent credit assignment, and human-in-the-loop counterfactual reasoning while jointly handling the difficulty of learning correct SCMs from interaction remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients (COMA)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces counterfactual baselines for credit assignment in cooperative MARL.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on counterfactual credit assignment in multi-agent RL.

status_evidence.title: Causal Reinforcement Learning (Bareinboim)
status_evidence.claim: Active research program on integrating SCMs with RL; counterfactual decision-making remains an open challenge.
status_evidence.snippet: Causal RL lecture series and open problems on counterfactual inference in sequential decision-making.

status_evidence.title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists counterfactual decision-making in RL as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The broader problem is listed as open in a recent survey.
